groups.title: Inherently impersonal VNCs and fictitious subjects
groups.proposal: Recognize the exact inherently impersonal lexical stems, keep their grammatical subject fixed as third-person singular, and distinguish a fictitious subject from both a real referent and a missing subject.
groups.writingJob: Build an inherently impersonal VNC from any entered intransitive Source whose typed lexical analysis is selected, use known Canvas stems only as defaults and examples, force the empty third-person singular subject frame, and realize ordinary tense and sentence material without creating a personal subject.
groups.readingJob: Show that the VNC is agentless but not subjectless, identify the grammatical subject as a nonreferential fiction, and present the licensed meteorological or event reading without treating an English gloss as grammar.
groups.decisionSplit: The user supplies the lexical stem and ordinary tense or mood. The application recognizes an inherently impersonal stem and fixes its subject automatically; there is no personal-versus-impersonal switch for a stem that can occur only impersonally.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse stem, tense, mood, polarity, and sentence controls; do not add fictitious-subject, third-person, agentless, meteorological, or supplementability switches.

groups.title: Nonanimate subjects are not impersonal subjects
groups.proposal: Keep a specific nonanimate common-number subject separate from a truly impersonal subject: both use third-person singular morphology, but only the nonanimate subject has an identifiable referent and can be supplemented.
groups.writingJob: Preserve the third-person singular surface shared by both constructions while using typed referent and supplementation structure to keep a nonanimate common-number subject personal and an empty impersonal subject unsupplementable.
groups.readingJob: Show whether the subject refers to one or more nameable nonanimate entities or to no entity at all, and explain why visible singular morphology does not erase common number or authorize an impersonal reading.
groups.decisionSplit: The user supplies an actual subject supplement or referential context when one is intended. The application combines that structure with lexical Source authority; merely omitting a visible supplement never turns an ordinary nonanimate subject into an impersonal one.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse subject supplement and referent cues; do not add singular-versus-common-number, nameability, supplementability, or nonanimate-versus-impersonal switches.

groups.title: Transform an active VNC into impersonal voice
groups.proposal: When impersonal voice is genuinely available, replace the active personal subject with a faceless third-person singular subject, derive the nonactive stem, allow intransitive or eligible transitive Sources, and reject a Source with a specific projective object while allowing reflexive or nonspecific objects.
groups.writingJob: Validate the active Source, discard its personal subject, import the fixed impersonal subject, derive the owner-issued nonactive stem, preserve eligible valence, and block specific projective-object Sources without confusing the result with passive voice.
groups.readingJob: Show the unrecoverable source subject, the faceless but existent general agent, the general or total human readings, and the exact difference from inherent impersonal and passive constructions.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses impersonal voice only when the active Source permits a genuine active, passive, or impersonal presentation choice. The application performs subject replacement, nonactive formation, and object-eligibility checks automatically.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse active Source, Voice, Valence, and object controls; do not add faceless-agent, replace-subject, derive-nonactive, generality, totality, or passive-versus-impersonal repair switches.

groups.writingJob: Preserve intransitive or transitive formula shape, install the fixed impersonal subject, discard the source subject without a recoverable trace, and reuse owner-issued ordinary or suppletive nonactive stems in their licensed tense cells.
groups.readingJob: Show active and impersonal formulas side by side, preserve the full range of general-human readings, and explain inherited irregular tense and meaning dislocation.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses ordinary tense and sentence coordinates. Source valence, impersonal subject, nonactive stem, and any irregular cell are automatic consequences of the typed Source.
